chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Umar ibn Ali ibn Umar ibn Yazeed from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar from one who narrated to him that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was saying:
The one who believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not enter the bathhouse except with a loin cloth.
Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Muhammad ibn Ja'far from one of his men from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so he would look at his nakedness.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not for the parents that they should look at the private part of the children, and it is not for the children that they should look at the nakedness of the parents.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) cursed the onlooker and the one looked at in the bathhouse, without a trouser.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on entering the bathhouse with family members?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia emphasis on *satr* (covering) and *haya* (modesty) within the communal space of the bathhouse, linking physical modesty to spiritual piety. It establishes a specific legal boundary where parents and children, despite their close kinship, must guard their *awrah* from one another to prevent the loss of modesty, a principle underscored by the Prophet's curse on both the observer and the observed. This ruling reflects the broader Islamic ethic of maintaining dignity in semi-private settings, distinguishing between familial intimacy and public exposure.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Umar Bin Ali Bin Umar Bin Yazeed, from his uncle Muhammad Bin Umar, from one who narrated it that, 
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘
The one who was a believer in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Last Day, so he should not enter the bathhouse except with a loin cloth’.

Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from one of his men, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The man should not enter the bathhouse along with his son, so he would look at his nakedness’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not for the parent that they should look at the private part of the children, and it is not the children that they should look at the nakedness of the parents’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> cursed the onlooker and the one looked at in the bathhouse, without a trouser’.
en.sarwar: 34. Certain persons of our people have narrated from ibn Jumhur from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Do not lie down in a bathhouse; it melts the fat of the kidneys.’”
